meta.title: Global Coffee Varieties Database — Merged v2
sources: Ardakilic Global Coffee Varieties Database v0 (120 entries)
Complete Global Coffee Types Database v1 (94 entries)
JARC (Jimma Agricultural Research Center) variety releases
Additional research: Reddit r/Coffee, specialty forums, academic papers

categories.name: Arabica — Heirloom & Landrace
categories.description: Ancient, unimproved Arabica varieties found in Ethiopia and Yemen. Genetic origin of virtually all cultivated coffee.

varieties.name: Typica
varieties.spread: Worldwide via Dutch / French colonial trade routes (1600s–1700s)
varieties.cup_profile: Delicate, sweet, clean, mild acidity, light-to-medium body
varieties.notes: The oldest cultivated Arabica variety; parent of Bourbon, Blue Mountain, Kona, and hundreds of other cultivars. Still grown in Papua New Guinea, Haiti, Peru, and Jamaica.

varieties.name: Bourbon
varieties.origin: Réunion Island (formerly Île Bourbon) — natural mutation of Typica
varieties.cup_profile: Complex sweetness, caramel, stone fruit, red apple, balanced acidity
varieties.notes: One of the most important Arabica varieties globally; parent of Caturra, Pacas, and many Brazilian cultivars.

varieties.name: Red Bourbon
varieties.cup_profile: Balanced sweetness, caramel, red fruit, mild citrus
varieties.notes: Standard Bourbon variety; red cherry ripening.

varieties.name: Yellow Bourbon
varieties.cup_profile: Sweeter than Red Bourbon, tropical fruit, lower acidity
varieties.notes: Yellow cherry ripening; widely grown in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Less common outside Brazil.

varieties.name: Orange Bourbon
varieties.cup_profile: Bright citrus, tropical, floral, complex
varieties.notes: Possibly a natural cross between Red and Yellow Bourbon; prized in specialty market.

varieties.name: Pink Bourbon
varieties.cup_profile: Intensely floral, jasmine, lychee, peach, candy sweetness
varieties.notes: Increasingly popular in specialty; genetic origin debated — may be cross of Red and Yellow Bourbon, or separate mutation. Commands high prices.

varieties.name: Gesha / Geisha
varieties.spread: Panama (via CATIE genebank, 1960s); now worldwide specialty
varieties.cup_profile: Jasmine, bergamot, peach, tropical fruit, rose, Earl Grey tea
varieties.notes: Most celebrated specialty variety in the world. Panama Gesha holds auction records over $10,000/kg. Ethiopian Gesha and Panamanian Gesha are distinct genetics despite the name.

varieties.name: Ethiopian Heirloom / Landrace
varieties.cup_profile: Extremely diverse — blueberry, wine, jasmine, tropical fruit, herbs
varieties.notes: Ethiopia is the genetic center of diversity for Coffea arabica. Thousands of distinct varieties exist; most are unnamed or listed simply as 'heirloom' on specialty bags.

varieties.name: Sudan Rume
varieties.spread: Research programs in Colombia, Central America
varieties.cup_profile: Intensely sweet, blackcurrant, stone fruit, complex
varieties.notes: Prized by breeders for exceptional cup quality and low caffeine. Used in breeding of Centroamericano. Rarely available commercially.

varieties.name: Mokka (Yemen Mokha)
varieties.spread: Yemen, Hawaii (Kona and Maui as Moka cultivar)
varieties.cup_profile: Intense chocolate, spice, wine, dried fruit
varieties.notes: Very small beans; naturally dwarf plant. Yemen's ancient traditional variety; historically exported through the port of Mokha giving coffee its name.

varieties.name: Laurina (Bourbon Pointu)
varieties.spread: Réunion, small pockets of Central America and New Caledonia
varieties.cup_profile: Delicate, mild, sweet, floral, low bitterness
varieties.notes: Naturally very low caffeine (~half of standard Arabica). Near-extinct historically; revival efforts on Réunion. Pointed cherry shape distinguishes it.

varieties.name: Kurume
varieties.cup_profile: Floral, jasmine, tea-like, citrus, delicate
varieties.notes: One of Ethiopia's most prized local landraces; increasingly marketed by name. Known for exceptional floral and tea-like qualities.

varieties.name: Wolisho
varieties.cup_profile: Stone fruit, citrus, winey, complex
varieties.notes: Common landrace in Sidama region; contributes balanced complexity to regional blends.

varieties.name: Dega
varieties.cup_profile: Berries, dark chocolate, herbal, sweet
varieties.notes: Important Ethiopian landrace; contributes body and chocolate notes to regional blends.

varieties.name: Chiroso
varieties.cup_profile: Intensely floral, jasmine, stone fruit, candy sweetness, complex
varieties.notes: Long misidentified as a Caturra mutation; DNA testing revealed distinct Ethiopian lineage. Became famous when Carmen Montoya won 2023 WBC prelims with Chiroso. Exclusively grown in Urrao, Colombia.

varieties.name: Bernardina
varieties.origin: Finca Los Bellotos, El Salvador (related to Ethiopian Agaro landraces)
varieties.cup_profile: Jasmine, peach, bergamot, honey, delicate — resembles Gesha
varieties.notes: Discovered at Finca Los Bellotos; originally mistaken for Gesha due to aromatic profile. DNA testing confirmed distinct variety related to Ethiopian Agaro landraces. Extremely rare; only a few farms grow it.

categories.name: Arabica — Improved & Selected Cultivars
categories.description: Selected, bred, or intentionally crossed varieties optimized for cup quality, yield, or disease resistance.

varieties.name: Caturra
varieties.origin: Minas Gerais, Brazil (natural dwarf mutation of Bourbon, discovered ~1915)
varieties.cup_profile: Bright citrus, clean, light body, lively acidity
varieties.notes: First compact Arabica cultivar; enabled higher-density planting. Still widely grown in Colombia and Central America despite vulnerability to leaf rust.

varieties.name: Catuaí
varieties.origin: Brazil (Mundo Novo × Caturra cross, IAC Campinas, 1949)
varieties.cup_profile: Soft, sweet, mild, nutty, low acidity
varieties.notes: One of the most planted varieties in Brazil. Strong branch structure resists fruit drop. Less complex than Bourbon or Typica but reliable.

varieties.name: Mundo Novo
varieties.origin: Brazil (Typica × Bourbon natural hybrid, discovered in São Paulo 1943)
varieties.cup_profile: Sweet, balanced, mild, clean
varieties.notes: Backbone of Brazilian coffee production for decades. Large plant suited to Brazil's lower-altitude farms. Parent of Catuaí.

varieties.name: SL28
varieties.origin: Kenya (selected by Scott Agricultural Laboratories from Tanganyika drought-resistant variety, 1931)
varieties.spread: Kenya, some Central American specialty farms
varieties.cup_profile: Intense blackcurrant, citrus, berry, wine, full body
varieties.notes: Widely regarded as one of the finest cup-quality varieties ever selected. Defines the classic 'Kenyan coffee' profile. Susceptible to coffee berry disease (CBD) and leaf rust.

varieties.name: SL34
varieties.origin: Kenya (selected from Loresho, a French Mission Bourbon derivative, 1935)
varieties.cup_profile: Citrus, peach, floral, bright structured acidity
varieties.notes: Often blended with SL28 in Kenyan lots. Performs well in higher-rainfall areas. Less common than SL28 in specialty market.

varieties.name: K7
varieties.origin: Kenya (Scott Labs selection from French Mission Bourbon)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, balanced, moderate acidity
varieties.notes: Older Kenyan selection; being replaced by Ruiru 11 and Batian in most farms.

varieties.name: Ruiru 11
varieties.origin: Kenya (Coffee Research Foundation, 1985 — complex hybrid including Timor Hybrid, SL28, N39, K7)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, acceptable but less complex than SL28/SL34
varieties.notes: Bred primarily for disease resistance and yield; specialty community often considers its cup inferior to SL28. Widely adopted by smallholder farmers.

varieties.name: Batian
varieties.origin: Kenya (Coffee Research Institute, 2010 — Ruiru 11 × SL28/SL34 back-cross)
varieties.cup_profile: Improved on Ruiru 11; approaching SL28 quality
varieties.notes: Named after a Kenyan peak. Bred to combine disease resistance with better cup quality than Ruiru 11.

varieties.name: Maragogipe (Maragogype)
varieties.origin: Maragogipe, Bahia, Brazil (natural giant-bean Typica mutation, ~1870)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, sweet, slightly earthy, low acidity
varieties.notes: Known as the 'elephant bean'; beans 2–3× normal size. Poor yield makes it uneconomical for most farmers. Notable curiosity in specialty market.

varieties.name: Pacas
varieties.origin: El Salvador (natural Bourbon dwarf mutation, discovered 1949 by Pacas family)
varieties.cup_profile: Sweet, balanced, mild fruit, caramel
varieties.notes: El Salvador's primary Bourbon-family compact variety; parent of Pacamara. Similar to Caturra but suited to El Salvador's conditions.

varieties.name: Pacamara
varieties.cup_profile: Floral, dark chocolate, herbal, complex, full body
varieties.notes: Large, irregular beans; prized in Central American specialty market. Has won numerous Cup of Excellence competitions.

varieties.name: Villa Sarchi (Villalobos)
varieties.origin: Sarchi, Costa Rica (natural Bourbon dwarf mutation)
varieties.cup_profile: Bright, fruity, floral, wine notes
varieties.notes: Costa Rican compact Bourbon mutation; used in breeding of Sarchimor. Suited to high-altitude, windy conditions.

varieties.name: Kent
varieties.origin: India (Mysore, Kent Estate, 1920s — selected from Typica)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, balanced, low acidity
varieties.notes: First commercial leaf-rust resistant selection; historically important for Indian coffee production.

varieties.name: S795
varieties.origin: India (CCRI Mysore, 1940s — Kent × Liberica hybrid back-cross)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, clean, balanced
varieties.notes: Most widely planted variety in India's Arabica belt; also grown in Sumatra, Indonesia.

varieties.name: Blue Mountain
varieties.spread: Jamaica, Papua New Guinea, Kenya (as a named cultivar)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, sweet, clean, balanced, no bitterness
varieties.notes: Jamaica Blue Mountain is a protected designation of origin. Commands very high prices ($50–$80+/100g). Historically exported in wooden barrels to Japan.

varieties.name: Kona
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, sweet, clean, slight nuttiness
varieties.notes: Protected origin; 'Kona Blend' is legally only 10% Kona. 100% Kona coffee is among the most expensive origin coffees. Grown in unique volcanic soil microclimate.

varieties.name: Maracaturra
varieties.cup_profile: Sweet, fruity, balanced, medium complexity
varieties.notes: Large-bean variety like its Maragogipe parent; grown in Nicaragua and Honduras.

varieties.name: Castillo
varieties.origin: Colombia (CENICAFÉ, 2005 — Caturra × Timor Hybrid back-cross program)
varieties.cup_profile: Balanced, sweet, mild citrus, clean
varieties.notes: Colombia's primary commercial variety since leaf rust devastated older plantings. Specialty community divided on cup quality vs. SL28/Caturra.

varieties.name: Colombia
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, clean, balanced
varieties.notes: Predecessor to Castillo; first leaf-rust resistant Colombian variety.

varieties.name: Tabi
varieties.cup_profile: Excellent cup quality; fruity, sweet, complex
varieties.notes: 'Tabi' means 'good' in Guambiano language. Combines superior cup quality with rust resistance — rare trait. Growing specialty interest.

varieties.name: Catimor
varieties.spread: Vietnam, Indonesia, India, Central America, East Africa
varieties.cup_profile: Often earthy, harsh, medicinal at lower altitudes; can be mild to good at high altitude
varieties.notes: Timor Hybrid introduced Robusta genetics; controversial in specialty due to cup quality. Vietnam's main Arabica cultivar. Many regional sub-lines (T5175, T8667, Linie S, etc.).

varieties.name: Sarchimor
varieties.spread: Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, India (as S1, S2, S4, S6)
varieties.cup_profile: Better than Catimor; clean, balanced, mild
varieties.notes: Parent of several named varieties: Marsellesa, Lempira, IHCAFE 90, Obatã. Generally better cup than Catimor-based crosses.

varieties.name: Marsellesa
varieties.origin: CIRAD France / PROMECAFE (Sarchimor × Villa Sarchi T3751 × Caturra)
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, clean, sweet, balanced
varieties.notes: Commercial hybrid for Central America; bred by CIRAD.

varieties.name: Lempira
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, acceptable specialty cup
varieties.notes: Honduras' most planted variety; named after an indigenous chief.

varieties.name: IHCAFE 90
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, balanced
varieties.notes: Often used interchangeably with Lempira in Honduras; both are Sarchimor selections.

varieties.name: Centroamericano (H3)
varieties.origin: CATIE, Costa Rica (Sudan Rume × Timor Hybrid T17, 2010s)
varieties.cup_profile: Exceptional — floral, fruity, complex, resembles Gesha in good conditions
varieties.notes: Exciting new variety combining Sudan Rume's cup quality with disease resistance. Increasingly winning Cup of Excellence competitions.

varieties.name: Obatã
varieties.cup_profile: Soft, sweet, mild, clean
varieties.notes: IAC Campinas selection combining disease resistance with Bourbon-like cup. Growing in Brazilian specialty market.

varieties.name: Tupi
varieties.cup_profile: Soft, sweet, balanced
varieties.notes: Brazilian commercial variety with rust resistance; bred by IAC.

varieties.name: Arusha
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, sweet, floral, citrus
varieties.notes: Named after Tanzania's Arusha region; similar genetics to Typica. Grown on Kilimanjaro and Meru slopes.

varieties.name: Jackson (Mibirizi)
varieties.origin: Burundi / Rwanda (Bourbon selection from 1930s Belgian missionaries)
varieties.cup_profile: Juicy, stone fruit, tropical, floral
varieties.notes: Bourbon-derivative grown in the volcanic soils of the Great Lakes region. Defines Burundian and Rwandan specialty coffee character.

varieties.name: 74110 (JARC Selection)
varieties.cup_profile: Citrus, floral, very clean, delicate
varieties.notes: Released 1979 from JARC selections. Increasingly common in single-variety Ethiopian specialty lots.

varieties.name: 74112 (JARC Selection)
varieties.cup_profile: Stone fruit, honey, balanced acidity
varieties.notes: Released 1979; selected for disease resistance and cup quality. Common in specialty microlots.

varieties.name: 74158 (JARC Selection)
varieties.cup_profile: Berry jam, winey, rich, complex
varieties.notes: Released 1979; known for rich berry character. Frequently appears in Guji and Sidama lots.

varieties.name: Starmaya
varieties.cup_profile: Good to very good; sweet, balanced, clean
varieties.notes: First F1 hybrid propagated by seed (not grafting). Combines high yield, disease resistance, and good cup.

varieties.name: Milenio (H10)
varieties.cup_profile: Very good; fruity, floral, high quality
varieties.notes: Part of WCR/CATIE F1 hybrid series; T5296 × Ethiopian landrace. Exceptional cup for a disease-resistant hybrid.

varieties.name: Casiopea
varieties.cup_profile: Good to very good; balanced, sweet
varieties.notes: F1 hybrid; good cup quality for a high-yielding disease-resistant plant.

varieties.name: Sidra
varieties.cup_profile: Tropical fruit, red apple, intense acidity, complex, wine-like
varieties.notes: Believed to be a Bourbon × Typica × Ethiopian heirloom hybrid. Not in WCR catalog. Prized for complex tropical fruit acidity. Used by multiple WBC competitors. Increasingly sold as a named variety.

categories.name: Robusta (Coffea canephora)
categories.description: Second-largest traded coffee species. Higher caffeine, lower altitude requirements, stronger disease resistance than Arabica.

varieties.name: Robusta (Coffea canephora var. robusta)
varieties.spread: Vietnam, Indonesia, Uganda, India, Ivory Coast, Philippines
varieties.cup_profile: Strong, earthy, rubbery, dark, bitter, tobacco
varieties.notes: Approximately 40% of world coffee production. Essential for espresso blends (crema, intensity), instant coffee, and Vietnamese ca phe. Twice the caffeine of Arabica.

varieties.name: Coffea canephora var. nganda (Kouillou)
varieties.cup_profile: Harsh, intensely bitter, very woody
varieties.notes: Wild sub-variety of Canephora; spreading rather than erect. Less commercially cultivated.

varieties.name: Conillon (Conilon)
varieties.cup_profile: Nutty, bold, lower bitterness than standard Robusta
varieties.notes: Brazil's main Robusta; used in domestic espresso blends. Considered a distinct variety from central African Robusta.

varieties.name: Specialty Robusta / Fine Robusta
varieties.origin: Uganda (Mount Elgon / Rwenzori), Vietnam (Dak Lak highlands)
varieties.cup_profile: Dark chocolate, tobacco, walnut, pepper, low bitterness
varieties.notes: Grown at higher altitudes than conventional Robusta; gaining specialty recognition. WCR and SCA have established Fine Robusta standards. Uganda produces exceptional examples.

varieties.name: Timor Hybrid (Hibrido de Timor / HDT)
varieties.spread: Breeding programs worldwide (Portugal, Colombia, India, Brazil)
varieties.cup_profile: Variable; often earthy, harsh; introgression used for breeding only
varieties.notes: Not commercially grown for its own cup quality; genetically critical as the source of leaf-rust resistance in most modern hybrid varieties (Catimor, Sarchimor, Castillo, Colombia).

varieties.name: BA-10 (Vietnamese Robusta clone)
varieties.cup_profile: Bold, bitter, earthy
varieties.notes: Vietnam's most planted Robusta clone; dominant in the world's largest Robusta-producing country.

categories.name: Liberica, Excelsa & Rare Species
categories.description: Lesser-known coffee species with niche but growing importance. Together represent ~1–2% of global production.

varieties.name: Liberica (Coffea liberica)
varieties.cup_profile: Floral, woody, smoky, jackfruit, full-bodied, slightly harsh
varieties.notes: Unique irregular, large beans. Briefly replaced Arabica after 1890s leaf rust devastation in Philippines. 'Barako' (Filipino Liberica) is a beloved national symbol.

varieties.name: Excelsa (Coffea liberica var. dewevrei)
varieties.spread: Philippines, Vietnam, SE Asia, parts of Africa
varieties.cup_profile: Tart, dark, fruity, winey, funky, complex
varieties.notes: Reclassified as a Liberica variant in 2006. Used in Philippines to add complexity and depth to blends. Growing specialty interest.

varieties.name: Coffea Stenophylla
varieties.cup_profile: Sweet, berry, stone fruit, complex — described as 'tastes like Arabica'
varieties.notes: Rediscovered wild in Sierra Leone in 2018 by researchers (Davis et al.). Highly heat-tolerant (survives at lower altitudes than Arabica); potential climate-change resilience candidate.

varieties.name: Coffea Racemosa
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, grassy, herbal, neutral
varieties.notes: Extremely low caffeine — one of the lowest of any Coffea species. Highly drought-tolerant. Being studied for climate adaptation and caffeine-free crossing.

varieties.name: Coffea Eugenioides
varieties.cup_profile: Sweet, caramel, very low caffeine, smooth
varieties.notes: Progenitor species of Coffea arabica (along with Robusta). Naturally very low caffeine. Being commercially explored by a few specialty producers in Colombia.

varieties.name: Coffea Charrieriana
varieties.cup_profile: Unknown / under study
varieties.notes: First naturally caffeine-free Coffea species discovered (2008, Cameroon). Not commercially viable but important for breeding decaffeinated varieties.

varieties.name: Coffea Canephora × Liberica (Hybrid)
varieties.cup_profile: Variable / experimental
varieties.notes: Experimental crosses being studied for climate resilience and disease resistance.

varieties.name: Coffea Congensis
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, neutral, low bitterness, slightly fruity
varieties.notes: One of few Coffea species that tolerates flooding. Being studied for climate adaptation.

categories.name: Processing & Fermentation Styles
categories.description: Post-harvest processing methods that profoundly shape the final cup regardless of variety.

varieties.name: Natural (Dry) Process
varieties.regions: Ethiopia, Yemen, Brazil, El Salvador, Indonesia
varieties.cup_profile: Fruity, winey, jammy, strawberry, blueberry, tropical fruit, heavy sweetness
varieties.drying_method: Dried whole cherry on raised beds or patios
varieties.notes: Oldest processing method; no water used. Higher risk of defects if poorly managed; exceptional when done well. Ethiopia Naturals (Yirgacheffe, Guji) are iconic examples.

varieties.name: Washed (Wet) Process
varieties.regions: Colombia, Ethiopia (Yirgacheffe washed), Kenya, Central America, Rwanda
varieties.cup_profile: Clean, bright, nuanced, transparent terroir expression, citrus, florals
varieties.notes: Pulp removed mechanically before drying; mucilage removed by fermentation and washing. Best for showcasing variety and terroir. Standard in East Africa and Colombia.

varieties.name: Yellow Honey Process
varieties.cup_profile: Slightly fruity, sweet, balanced, minimal fermentation notes
varieties.notes: Least mucilage of honey variants retained; cleaner than Red/Black Honey; more fruit than Washed.

varieties.name: Red Honey Process
varieties.cup_profile: Juicy, fruity, caramel, balanced
varieties.notes: Half of mucilage retained; moderate fruit character with good sweetness.

varieties.name: Black Honey Process
varieties.cup_profile: Intense fruit, wine-like, very sweet, complex
varieties.notes: Nearly all mucilage retained; closest to Natural in profile while still being a Honey process.

varieties.name: Wet-Hulled (Giling Basah)
varieties.cup_profile: Earthy, cedar, tobacco, dark chocolate, mushroom, full body, very low acidity
varieties.notes: Unique to Indonesia; beans hulled at ~50% moisture content (instead of standard ~12%), resulting in distinctive blue-green appearance and earthy flavor. Classic Sumatran profile.

varieties.name: Anaerobic Natural
varieties.regions: Colombia, Ethiopia, Costa Rica, Panama, Honduras
varieties.cup_profile: Intense tropical fruit, bubblegum, fermented sweetness, wine, extreme complexity
varieties.fermentation: Sealed-tank anaerobic fermentation of whole cherry (24–200 hours)
varieties.notes: Fermented in sealed oxygen-free tanks; produces extremely distinct and polarizing flavor profiles. Dominant in competition coffee.

varieties.name: Anaerobic Washed
varieties.cup_profile: Clean but unusual fermentation notes; whiskey, tropical, bright
varieties.fermentation: Sealed-tank anaerobic fermentation before pulping and washing
varieties.notes: Combines anaerobic fermentation with washed processing for cleaner but still adventurous cup.

varieties.name: Carbonic Maceration
varieties.origin: Wine industry; adapted to coffee ~2015 by Sasa Sestic
varieties.cup_profile: Sparkling, bright, cherry cola, clean fermentation, unique complexity
varieties.notes: Sasa Sestic won 2015 World Barista Championship with this method. Borrowed directly from Beaujolais wine production.

varieties.name: Lactic Fermentation
varieties.cup_profile: Creamy, yogurt-like, clean sweetness, low acidity
varieties.fermentation: Anaerobic; conditions favor lactic acid bacteria
varieties.notes: Temperature and water levels managed to promote lactic acid bacteria dominance in fermentation.

varieties.name: Washed Natural (Semi-Washed / Pulped Natural)
varieties.cup_profile: Body of Natural, cleanliness of Washed; sweet, balanced
varieties.notes: Cherry pulped but mucilage not washed off; dried as-is. Brazilian standard process.

varieties.name: Yeast-Inoculated Fermentation
varieties.cup_profile: Precise, consistent, controlled fruit and floral notes
varieties.fermentation: Specific yeast strains (wine, beer, bakery) inoculated into fermentation tank
varieties.notes: Adding commercial yeast strains to fermentation to produce predictable, reproducible flavor. Controversial in competition; some classes permit it, others do not.

varieties.name: Koji Fermentation
varieties.cup_profile: Umami, miso, soy sauce, savory-sweet, unprecedented complexity
varieties.fermentation: Koji mold (Aspergillus oryzae) inoculated onto coffee cherry/mucilage
varieties.notes: Breakthrough technique borrowed from Japanese sake/soy sauce. Koji enzymes produce unique umami compounds. Extremely experimental.

varieties.name: Thermal Shock Process
varieties.cup_profile: Intense fruit, candy sweetness, clean, no ferment defects
varieties.fermentation: Rapid temperature cycling (hot/cold) after anaerobic fermentation
varieties.notes: Pioneered by Diego Bermudez; uses rapid hot/cold water cycling to lock in fruit flavors while eliminating fermentation defects.

varieties.name: Fruit Co-Fermentation
varieties.regions: Colombia, Costa Rica, specialty farms worldwide
varieties.cup_profile: Intense fruit infusion; strawberry, passionfruit, peach, wine, highly aromatic
varieties.fermentation: Fruit must, yeast strains, spices, or hops added during sealed-tank anaerobic fermentation
varieties.notes: Fruit musts, spices, or hops are co-fermented with coffee cherry or mucilage in anaerobic tanks. Creates intensely fruity, unconventional profiles. Growing trend in specialty; some controversy over transparency in competitions.

categories.name: Commercially Known Names & Specialty Lots
categories.description: Coffees known by trade, origin, or estate names rather than botanical variety names.

varieties.name: Panama Gesha (Hacienda La Esmeralda)
varieties.cup_profile: Jasmine, bergamot, peach, tropical, mandarin
varieties.notes: Hacienda La Esmeralda sparked the global Gesha revolution in 2004. Annual Best of Panama auction lot.

varieties.name: Yirgacheffe (Washed)
varieties.cup_profile: Jasmine, lemon verbena, bergamot, tea-like, delicate
varieties.notes: Benchmark for washed Ethiopian coffee; Yirgacheffe W2 grade most common specialty version.

varieties.name: Yirgacheffe (Natural)
varieties.cup_profile: Blueberry jam, strawberry, wine, floral
varieties.notes: Natural-processed version of Yirgacheffe; more fruit-driven than washed counterpart.

varieties.name: Sidama / Sidamo
varieties.cup_profile: Berry, citrus, chocolate, balanced complexity
varieties.notes: Sidama became Ethiopia's first protected origin via WTO in 2021.

varieties.name: Harrar (Harar)
varieties.cup_profile: Winey, blueberry, dark chocolate, earthy, intense
varieties.notes: Ancient trading city; dry-processed at high altitude. Mocha-Harrar is a classic blend component.

varieties.name: Guji
varieties.cup_profile: Stone fruit, floral, tropical, clean
varieties.notes: Formerly sold as Yirgacheffe or Sidama; given its own regional identity in recent years.

varieties.name: Sumatra Mandheling
varieties.origin: Mandailing Batak highlands, North Sumatra, Indonesia
varieties.cup_profile: Earthy, cedar, dark chocolate, low acidity, full body, syrupy
varieties.notes: Mandheling is a trade name, not a village; processed by wet-hulling method unique to Indonesia.

varieties.name: Sumatra Lintong
varieties.cup_profile: Earthy, herbal, tobacco, less intense than Mandheling
varieties.notes: Grown near Lake Toba; considered slightly cleaner than Mandheling.

varieties.name: Sulawesi Toraja
varieties.cup_profile: Dark chocolate, black pepper, earthy, full
varieties.notes: Grown by Toraja ethnic group; famous for elaborate funeral ceremonies and unique coffee character.

varieties.name: Kopi Luwak
varieties.origin: Indonesia (Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi, Bali); also Philippines (Kape Alamid)
varieties.cup_profile: Earthy, smooth, low bitterness, mild, chocolatey
varieties.processing: Civet-processed (passes through Asian palm civet digestive system)
varieties.notes: Most expensive widely traded coffee. Fermentation by civet enzymes reduces bitterness. Serious animal welfare concerns around caged civets; wild-sourced versions exist.

varieties.name: Black Ivory Coffee
varieties.cup_profile: Smooth, low bitterness, earthy, hint of fruit, tamarind
varieties.notes: World's most expensive coffee; passed through Asian elephant digestive system. Produced by Black Ivory Coffee Company in Golden Triangle. Portion of proceeds funds elephant welfare.

varieties.name: Jamaican Blue Mountain
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, clean, sweet, balanced, no defects
varieties.notes: Protected Designation of Origin; sold in traditional wooden barrels; 80%+ exported to Japan.

varieties.name: Hawaiian Kona Extra Fancy
varieties.origin: Kona district, Big Island, Hawaii, USA
varieties.cup_profile: Mild, sweet, light nutty, clean
varieties.notes: Extra Fancy is highest grade; beans must be ≥19/64 inch screen. Grown in 'the coffee belt' between Hualalai and Mauna Loa volcanoes.

varieties.name: Yemen Mocha
varieties.cup_profile: Winey, blueberry, dark fruit, chocolate, spice
varieties.notes: Origin of the word 'mocha'; has been naturally dry-processed for centuries. Ongoing conflict has disrupted production. Among the world's most historically significant coffees.

varieties.name: Panama Geisha (Finca Deborah)
varieties.cup_profile: Jasmine, bergamot, peach, candied lemon, extraordinary clarity
varieties.notes: One of the highest-altitude Gesha farms in Panama. Multiple Best of Panama wins. Ultra-clean profiles.

varieties.name: Finca El Paraíso (Diego Bermudez)
varieties.cup_profile: Intense tropical fruit, candy sweetness, extraordinary complexity from advanced processing
varieties.processing: Thermal Shock, Anaerobic, Yeast-inoculated (pioneer of advanced methods)
varieties.notes: Diego Bermudez is one of the most innovative coffee processors globally. Pioneer of thermal shock processing. Multiple competition wins. Coffees sold by farm name with specific lot codes as branded products.
